learn.title: Pricing calculator, tags and cost scenarios
objectives: Use the Azure pricing calculator to estimate costs before deploying.
Know what affects an estimate: region, tier, quantity, hours, reservations, support.
Describe resource tags and their uses, especially cost allocation.
Know how tags behave: not inherited by default, but Azure Policy can apply or inherit them.
Choose the right tool: pricing calculator (estimate) or Cost Management (actual spend).
concepts: Azure pricing calculator
Free web tool that estimates the monthly cost of Azure services before you deploy them. No Azure account needed.
Estimate
The calculator's output is an estimate, not a quote or a bill. Actual cost depends on real usage.
Estimate options
Region, service tier or size, quantity, hours of use, reservation or savings plan term, licensing, and support plan.
Saving and sharing
Estimates can be saved (when signed in), exported to Excel, or shared by link.
TCO calculator
Compares on-premises costs with Azure. It's not in the current exam objectives; it's supporting context only.
Tag
A name-value pair, such as Environment=Production, applied to subscriptions, resource groups or resources.
Tag uses
Cost allocation, operations, security classification, governance and compliance, and automation.
Tag inheritance
Resources don't inherit tags from their resource group or subscription by default. Azure Policy can add, require or inherit tags.
Tag limit
Each resource, resource group or subscription supports up to 50 tag name-value pairs.
Cost by tag
Cost Management can group and filter costs by tag, for example by CostCenter.
comparisons: The calculator estimates future, planned costs. Cost Management shows actual and forecast spending on deployed resources.
A resource is in exactly one resource group, but it can carry many tags that cut across groups and subscriptions.
A tag is metadata. A policy enforces rules, such as requiring a tag or copying one from the resource group.
The pricing calculator estimates Azure service costs. The TCO calculator compares an on-premises estate with Azure (not in current objectives).
traps: The pricing calculator doesn't show what you've already spent.
An estimate isn't a guaranteed price.
Tags don't restrict access or deployments by themselves.
You don't need an Azure subscription to use the pricing calculator.
revision: Planning a cost? Use the pricing calculator.
Checking real spend? Use Cost Management.
Region and tier change the estimate.
Tags = name-value metadata for organising and allocating cost.
Use Azure Policy to require or inherit tags.
